title: Noor and the Summer
premise: Ines Ishikawa, a wedding planner who swore off love after her fiancé's betrayal, is forced to run a summer pen-pal program for a coastal town's centennial festival. A clerical error pairs her with Daniel Voss, the developer whose demolition of her family's orchard once left her family destitute — and neither knows who is on the other end of the letters. As anonymous confessions deepen into real intimacy, Ines discovers Daniel is secretly fighting his own inheritance: his dying father's empire, built on the same land grab that ruined her. When identities are revealed mid-festival, Ines must choose between legal vengeance and a justice of her own making — reclaiming the orchard through the town's old covenant law — and risk loving wholeheartedly before the summer, and Daniel's father, run out of time. The book ends with the orchard restored as a public trust and Ines planning one last wedding: her own.
about_author: Rafael Almeida is the pen name of a former small-town journalist who spent a decade covering land disputes along the Atlantic coast before turning to fiction. He writes romances about people who learn that justice and tenderness are not opposites.

chapters.title: The Last Wedding She'll Ever Plan
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She orchestrates a flawless society wedding while privately drafting her resignation from love itself, haunted by flashbacks of her broken engagement and her family's lost orchard. The festival committee ambushes her afterward with the pen-pal program she can't refuse. Emotional beat: armored competence cracking into dread.

chapters.title: A Clerical Error
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. He signs up for the pen-pal program only to soften his image before the centennial development vote; a volunteer's typo routes him to Ines instead of a stranger. His first letter is corporate spin; hers is acid. Emotional beat: irritation masking curiosity on both sides.

chapters.title: Letters Unsigned
chapters.summary: Alternating POV via letters. Anonymous, they begin confessing things neither would say face-to-face: Ines admits she still grieves the orchard; Daniel admits he hates what he builds. In daylight they spar at committee meetings, unaware. Emotional beat: the dangerous intimacy of strangers.

chapters.title: What the Orchard Gave
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Sorting her late grandmother's papers for the festival archive, she finds the original land covenant hinting the Voss purchase was never fully legal. Meanwhile a letter arrives that sounds eerily like Daniel's voice. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Son Who Inherits Everything
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. His father's illness worsens, and the old man demands he fast-track the festival-site demolition — the same ground Ines is restoring. Daniel stalls, writing truths in letters he can't say aloud. Emotional beat: filial duty curdling into quiet rebellion.

chapters.title: Midsummer, Unmasked
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the festival's letter-reading ceremony, a volunteer reads their correspondence aloud; phrasing betrays them both. Public revelation, private devastation — Ines sees the enemy's name where a friend should be. Emotional beat: betrayal at maximum volume.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She nearly hands the covenant to a rival lawyer who'd gut the whole valley, then pulls back — justice outside the law must still be just. Daniel, cut off by his father, offers testimony against his own company. Emotional beat: choosing principle over revenge.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Before the town council, Daniel exposes the forged signatures behind the original sale, sacrificing his inheritance and his father's last approval. Ines watches, unmoved by victory, moved by him. Emotional beat: ruin as redemption.

chapters.title: Everything I Didn't Write
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. With the covenant upheld and the orchard declared a public trust, Ines retreats into old armor, terrified to lend pieces of her heart again. Daniel leaves one final letter — unsigned no more — at her door. Emotional beat: fear meeting its match.

chapters.title: Noor and the Summer
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Named for the lantern festival closing the season, the finale brings the town to the reclaimed orchard. Ines reads Daniel's letter aloud, answers it in person, and agrees to plan one more wedding — theirs — under the first trees replanted. Emotional beat: wholehearted risk rewarded.
